meta.tagline: A no-hype field guide to learning AI with official, free resources.

resources.title: Introduction to Generative AI
resources.description: A 45-minute, no-code explanation of what generative AI is, how it differs from traditional machine learning, and where Google uses it. Finish with a short quiz and a free Google skill badge.
resources.certificateNote: Free Google skill badge after passing the quiz; a Google Skills account is required.

resources.title: Generative AI Fundamentals
resources.description: A free one-hour on-demand course on core generative AI concepts, high-value business use cases, model trade-offs, governance, and where agents fit. Pass the quiz to earn a Databricks badge for LinkedIn and your résumé.
resources.certificateNote: Free one-hour training; pass the quiz to earn a Databricks badge. A Databricks account is required.

resources.title: Generative AI for Educators with Gemini
resources.description: A free two-hour, self-paced course for middle- and high-school educators who want to save time on everyday tasks, personalize instruction, and use Gemini and NotebookLM responsibly. No previous AI experience is required.
resources.certificateNote: Free two-hour course with a certificate for professional-development credit, subject to district and state rules.

resources.title: Elements of AI: Introduction to AI
resources.description: A gentle, non-technical course from the University of Helsinki and MinnaLearn. Learn what AI can and cannot do, where it shows up in daily life, and how it affects society. No math or coding required.
resources.certificateNote: The course is free; an optional certificate costs €50.

resources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
resources.description: Google's interactive tour of machine learning fundamentals: regression, classification, neural networks, large language models, and fairness. Videos, readings, and hands-on exercises make it a strong free foundation.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is listed; it is an open Google learning resource.

resources.title: AI for Beginners
resources.description: Microsoft's open 12-week, 24-lesson curriculum covers AI history, neural networks, computer vision, natural language processing, and ethics, with quizzes and labs. Take only the lessons you need.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is offered for this open curriculum.

resources.title: Generative AI for Beginners
resources.description: Twenty-one lessons that move from prompt basics to retrieval-augmented generation, agents, and responsible use, with Python code samples. You can read the ideas without using Azure, though a little coding helps.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is offered for this open curriculum.

resources.title: Ollama Quickstart
resources.description: An official quickstart for running open models locally: install Ollama, pull a model, connect a desktop app or coding agent, and make a first local API request without sending prompts to a hosted service.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate; a working local model and a short setup note are the evidence.

resources.title: Fundamentals of Generative AI
resources.description: A three-hour AWS Skill Builder course on generative AI, natural language processing, and choosing an AI/ML approach for a real use case. The digital course is free; hands-on labs may require a paid subscription.
resources.certificateNote: The digital course is free; AWS offers free digital badges for selected Skill Builder learning. Check the current course page and badge catalogue.

resources.title: AI Python for Beginners
resources.description: A friendly 11.5-hour introduction to Python with an AI helper. Cover variables, functions, data, and small projects; no coding background required. The lessons are free, and the pace is yours.
resources.certificateNote: Lessons are free; a certificate requires DeepLearning.AI PRO membership.

resources.title: ChatGPT Prompt Engineering for Developers
resources.description: A 1 hour 40 minute course on writing clear instructions, summarizing, inferring, transforming, and expanding text with an LLM API. Basic Python is helpful, but the prompting principles apply far beyond code.
resources.certificateNote: Lessons are free; a certificate requires DeepLearning.AI PRO membership.

resources.title: GitHub Copilot Fundamentals Part 1 of 2
resources.description: A free, nine-module path on using GitHub Copilot responsibly: plan choices, prompt engineering, Copilot Spaces, advanced features, IDE and command-line use, developer workflows, and unit testing with an AI assistant.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is issued for this learning path; Microsoft Learn tracks module completion.

resources.title: AI for Everyone
resources.description: Andrew Ng's non-technical course on what AI can do, how to spot useful opportunities, and how AI projects get built. Coursera now offers a free preview of the first module; full access and a certificate are paid.
resources.certificateNote: Coursera preview is free and does not include a certificate. Full course and certificate require payment or approved financial aid.

resources.title: Machine Learning Specialization
resources.description: Andrew Ng's three-course foundation in supervised learning, advanced learning algorithms, and unsupervised learning or recommender systems. Preview the first module free; graded labs and the certificate require payment or financial aid.
resources.certificateNote: The Coursera preview is free but does not include graded labs or a certificate. Paid enrollment or approved financial aid unlocks the full specialization.

resources.title: Kaggle: Python
resources.description: Five hours of hands-on Python in the browser: variables, functions, loops, lists, dictionaries, and importing libraries. Short coding exercises and a free completion certificate make it a low-friction first coding step.
resources.certificateNote: Free Kaggle Learn completion certificate after finishing the course exercises.

resources.title: Kaggle: Pandas
resources.description: Four hours of practical data wrangling with pandas: selecting, filtering, grouping, joining, and cleaning real tabular data. Finish with a free certificate and the skills to inspect a dataset without panic.
resources.certificateNote: Free Kaggle Learn completion certificate.

resources.title: GitHub Foundations Part 1 of 2
resources.description: A free, eight-module learning path covering Git and GitHub essentials: repositories, commits, branches, pull requests, Projects, Markdown, Codespaces, code scanning, and an introduction to GitHub Copilot. The certification exam is separate.
resources.cost: Free to learn; optional exam paid
resources.certificateNote: Free learning path. The separate GitHub Foundations certification exam is paid and priced by country.

resources.title: Kaggle: Intro to Machine Learning
resources.description: A three-hour first pass at machine learning with scikit-learn. Build a decision tree and random forest, use a train/test split, and learn why validation matters. No prior ML needed.
resources.certificateNote: Free Kaggle Learn completion certificate.

resources.title: Kaggle: Intermediate Machine Learning
resources.description: Move beyond a first model with missing-value handling, categorical variables, pipelines, cross-validation, and gradient boosting. Good next practice after Intro to Machine Learning.
resources.certificateNote: Free Kaggle Learn completion certificate.

resources.title: Kaggle: Intro to Deep Learning
resources.description: Use TensorFlow and Keras to build a first neural network, add layers, train with stochastic gradient descent, and recognize overfitting. Four focused hours with a free certificate attached.
resources.certificateNote: Free Kaggle Learn completion certificate.

resources.title: Kaggle: Intro to AI Ethics
resources.description: Four hours on human-centered design, fairness, and privacy for AI systems. The examples are practical, the language is plain, and you leave with a free certificate plus a better checklist for building responsibly.
resources.certificateNote: Free Kaggle Learn completion certificate.

resources.title: 5-Day AI Agents Intensive Course with Google
resources.description: A self-paced, hands-on agent program from Kaggle and Google: daily codelabs, whitepapers, a capstone project, and community discussion. It is free to follow; cohort-specific badges or certificates can change, so check the current guide.
resources.certificateNote: Cohort badges and certificates have changed between sessions. The official course guide is the source of truth.

resources.title: Scientific Computing with Python
resources.description: freeCodeCamp's project-heavy Python certification covers variables, loops, functions, objects, and algorithms, ending with five build projects and a free certification. The curriculum is large; do the first sections for a taste.
resources.certificateNote: Free freeCodeCamp certification after completing the required projects.

resources.title: Data Analysis with Python
resources.description: Learn NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn through lessons and five data-analysis projects, with a free certification at the end. A practical, long-form path for people who like to learn by building.
resources.certificateNote: Free freeCodeCamp certification after completing the required projects.

resources.title: Machine Learning with Python
resources.description: A long-form, project-based TensorFlow and Keras certification covering neural networks, classification, clustering, and recommender systems. Five projects lead to a free certificate; it is a marathon, not a weekend.
resources.certificateNote: Free freeCodeCamp certification after completing the required projects.

resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
resources.description: A free, twelve-chapter course on transformers, datasets, tokenizers, fine-tuning, and modern LLM techniques using the Hugging Face ecosystem. It expects good Python and benefits from an intro deep-learning course.
resources.certificateNote: Hugging Face states that this course does not currently offer certification.

resources.title: Hugging Face AI Agents Course
resources.description: A free course from beginner to agent builder. Learn tool use, agent loops, smolagents, LlamaIndex, and LangGraph, then build and share an agent. Basic Python is expected; two free certificate levels are available.
resources.certificateNote: Certification is free: a fundamentals certificate after Unit 1, or a completion certificate after assignments and the final challenge.

resources.title: Hugging Face MCP Course
resources.description: A free course built with Anthropic that explains the Model Context Protocol and walks you through building MCP applications. You should know basic AI, APIs, and either Python or TypeScript. Free certificates are available.
resources.certificateNote: Free fundamentals certificate after Unit 1; free completion certificate after the use-case units and assignments.

resources.title: AI Agents for Beginners
resources.description: Eighteen open lessons on agent design patterns, retrieval, tool use, multi-agent systems, and responsible development, with runnable samples. Basic coding helps, and there is no certificate or paywall.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is offered for this open curriculum.

resources.title: MCP for Beginners
resources.description: A free, open curriculum on Model Context Protocol fundamentals, security, and practical labs, with examples across multiple languages. Useful as a reference shelf while you build your first MCP server.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is offered for this open curriculum.

resources.title: MCP: Build Rich-Context AI Apps with Anthropic
resources.description: A focused two-hour short course on building applications with the Model Context Protocol, made with Anthropic. You should be comfortable with Python and basic LLM concepts. Lessons are free.
resources.certificateNote: Lessons are free; a certificate requires DeepLearning.AI PRO membership.

resources.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
resources.description: Jeremy Howard's nine-lesson, code-first course takes you from training a first model to deploying practical deep-learning projects. It is free and famously approachable, but it is not a first coding course.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is offered; the course emphasizes working projects.

resources.title: MIT Introduction to Deep Learning (6.S191)
resources.description: MIT's fast-paced introduction to deep learning: nine lectures and three software labs spanning vision, sequence models, generative AI, and more. The site labels it beginner-friendly, but calculus and linear algebra help.
resources.certificateNote: No certificate is listed; course materials are openly available.

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence with Python
resources.description: Harvard's seven-week course on search, knowledge, uncertainty, optimization, learning, neural networks, and language, with substantial Python projects. Audit for free; a verified certificate currently costs US$299.
resources.certificateNote: Free audit track, no certificate. A verified CS50 AI certificate currently costs US$299.

resources.title: Coursera's Free Course Preview, Explained
resources.description: Coursera's official announcement of the change from free audit to a first-module preview. Read this before trusting any list of 'free Coursera courses': previews do not earn certificates.
resources.certificateNote: Not a course.

resources.title: Coursera Financial Aid: How to Apply
resources.description: Coursera's official help article on applying for financial aid when you cannot pay for a certificate. Approval is not guaranteed, and processing takes time, but it is the legitimate route—not a third-party 'free certificate' hack.
resources.certificateNote: Not a course.

resources.title: What the Free edX Audit Track Includes
resources.description: edX's official explanation of audit versus verified enrollment. Audit is free but can be time-limited, excludes some graded work, and does not include a certificate. Verified certificates are paid.
resources.certificateNote: Not a course.

resources.title: AWS Digital Badges: How They Work
resources.description: AWS's official badge page explains how to earn and share digital badges, which are free to accept, and how they differ from paid AWS Certification exams. Good research before you chase a badge.
resources.certificateNote: Not a course.

resources.title: People + AI Guidebook
resources.description: Google's free, human-centered design guide for AI products. Work through chapters on mental models, explainability, feedback, errors, and trust—especially useful if you want to build tools people actually understand.
resources.certificateNote: Not a course.

resources.title: Prompt Engineering (Google Whitepaper)
resources.description: Google's free whitepaper on prompt engineering techniques, model settings, and real examples. It goes deeper than a list of magic phrases and gives you a vocabulary for why a prompt works.
resources.certificateNote: Not a course.

resources.title: Model Context Protocol Documentation
resources.description: The official open-standard documentation for MCP: architecture, servers, clients, tools, resources, and prompts. Use it as your reference when a course moves too fast, or when you are designing your own tool connection.
resources.certificateNote: Not a course.

resources.title: Machine Learning Yearning
resources.description: Andrew Ng's free ebook on shaping machine-learning projects: choosing metrics, prioritizing errors, and deciding what to improve next. Short chapters, little math, and unusually practical for beginners and managers.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to books.

resources.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
resources.description: A respected, approachable textbook on statistical learning, with free PDFs and companion labs in R and Python. It is a patient bridge from classical statistics to modern machine learning.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to books.

resources.title: Deep Learning for Coders with fastai and PyTorch
resources.description: The free online edition of Jeremy Howard and Sylvain Gugger's hands-on deep-learning book. It is the companion to the fast.ai course and assumes you can already code.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to books.

resources.title: Dive into Deep Learning
resources.description: An open, interactive deep-learning textbook that combines math, prose, and runnable code. Adopted by hundreds of universities; free online, with a print edition if you prefer paper.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to books.

resources.title: Deep Learning
resources.description: The canonical deep-learning reference by Goodfellow, Bengio, and Courville, free to read in HTML. It is rigorous and dense—a reference to grow into, not a first book for most beginners.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to books.

resources.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
resources.description: A free textbook that fills the math gaps behind machine learning: linear algebra, analytic geometry, probability, optimization, and modeling. Use selected chapters as a companion, not a prerequisite gate.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to books.

resources.title: 3Blue1Brown
resources.description: Visual, carefully paced explanations of neural networks, calculus, and linear algebra. Start with the neural-network series when jargon starts to blur; the animations build intuition faster than definitions alone.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: StatQuest with Josh Starmer
resources.description: Clear, cheerful explanations of statistics and machine-learning algorithms, from histograms to random forests and boosting. The songs are optional; the step-by-step diagrams are the reason to stay.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: Andrej Karpathy
resources.description: Deep, code-first explanations of language models, backpropagation, and building neural networks from scratch. Best when you have some Python and want to understand what is happening under the hood.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: freeCodeCamp.org
resources.description: Long-form, free full courses on Python, machine learning, and AI development, usually taught by working practitioners. Use the course chapters to sample a topic before committing to a 300-hour certification.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels; certifications live on freeCodeCamp.org.

resources.title: Hugging Face
resources.description: Practical demos and tutorials for models, datasets, agents, and open-source AI tooling. Useful when you want to see a workflow before reading the documentation.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: Google DeepMind
resources.description: Research talks, explainers, and glimpses of frontier AI work in science, models, and safety. A good channel for context on where the field is going—and what is still research, not a product.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: OpenAI
resources.description: Official product demonstrations, developer sessions, and conversations about how AI systems are built and used. Treat launch videos as a starting point; verify claims against documentation.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: Anthropic
resources.description: Official talks and demos about Claude, agentic systems, safety research, and building with MCP. Helpful context for the agent-building path, especially around evaluation and guardrails.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: DeepLearning.AI
resources.description: Lectures, course previews, and interviews about AI careers and building with LLMs. Useful for deciding which DeepLearning.AI course fits your next step.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: Microsoft Developer
resources.description: Developer-focused demos and deep dives on Azure AI, Copilot, agents, and open-source tooling. Look for the hands-on sessions where you can follow along with code.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: Google Cloud Tech
resources.description: Practical Google Cloud AI demos, Gemini walkthroughs, and engineering talks. Best used with a project in hand rather than watched passively.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.

resources.title: Kaggle
resources.description: Competition walkthroughs, agent course sessions, and practical data-science talks from Kaggle's community. Good for seeing how other people approach messy, real datasets.
resources.certificateNote: Not applicable to channels.
